newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 9.5 vs 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 9.5 vs 8.7 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 80 basis points to 9.5 percent on Monday despite good supply as costly term loans of savings banks pushed up otherwise steady prices.
Supply levelled off slightly but was still strong at 95 million kuna, against 47.3 million in demand.
The weighted call money rate stood at 7.2 percent.
One-month money varied between 13 and 15 percent and two-month funds for savings banks were granted at 19 percent.
Two-week interbank money was extended at 9.0 percent, while savings banks paid 16 percent for the same term loans.
Insurers rolled over their 40-day and one-month loans at 11 and 13.5 percent respectively.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday eased further to 7.0556 against the dollar but firmed to 3.5690 to the mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
